When you report what other people ask or command, you often make some grammar changes.
When we want to report an order, we usually use the following verbs: tell - command - order - forbid - ask - warn.
I wanted to know why you didn't tell me you were doing that.
If you asked whether or not I was going to, I would have been more than happy to tell you.
He mentioned that we could all do our part in making the office more environmentally and ergonomically friendly.
She asked me to come see her later.

When we want to report questions, we usually use the following verbs: ask - want to know - inquire.
How to report Yes / No questions :
When we report yes/no questions, we use "if" or "whether".

images.text:
Adam: Hey Kristi, what did you think about my presentation?
Kristi: I wanted to know why you didn't tell me you were doing that. I could have helped you!
Adam: I know you would if I told you. I didn't want to tell anyone what I was doing because I had wanted it to be a surprise.
Kristi: Ever since you admitted to taking my notes, you've been ignoring me. We don't chat like we used to. Seeing that you already apologized, I don't understand why you were ignoring me. I thought we came to a mutual understanding about the whole thing.

Adam: I'm sorry. I didn't mean to come across like this. As soon I started putting together my presentation, I just got so caught up with it. But now that I've finished with that, we can totally catch up. As soon as we're done work today, we'll go out out for some coffee.
Kristi: Not today, sorry. I have to prep for my interview.
Adam: Interview ... for what? Did you apply for the junior editor position? Why didn't you tell me?
Kristi: If you asked whether or not I was going to, I would have been more than happy to tell you.
Adam: I guess you're right. So, when's your interview?
Kristi: I sent in my application a few days ago. While I was waiting to hear from Denise about it, I received a phone call from Pamela, the recruitment officer. My interview is on Friday.
Adam: That's great news. Ever since Boris told us about the position, I knew you would be the perfect candidate for the job. I'm glad you applied.
Kristi: Thanks, Adam. Did you apply? I hope you did.

Adam: No, I'm definitely not cut out for it. You're better suited for it than I am. I was hoping that by me setting out to do this presentation, it would help me step up my game but I think it's done the opposite.
Kristi: It was a great presentation. You did a really good job. You mentioned how we could all do our part in making the office more environmentally and ergonomically friendly. It got everyone thinking. While walking to work, I thought about ways I could reduce my environmental footprint.
Adam: I don't know Kristi. I got called into Denise's office to talk to her about it. I think she might fire me.
